sections.title: 选词填空
paragraphs: “That which does not kill us makes us stronger.” But parents can’t handle it when teenagers put this [[26]] into practice. Now technology has become the new field for the age-old battle between adults and their freedom-seeking kids.

Locked indoors, unable to get on their bicycles and hang out with their friends, teens have turned to social media and their mobile phones to socialize with their peers. What they do online often [[27]] what they might otherwise do if their mobility weren’t so heavily [[28]] in the age of helicopter parenting. Social media and smart-phone apps have become so popular in recent years because teens need a place to call their own. They want the freedom to [[29]] their identity and the world around them. Instead of [[30]] out, they jump online.
As teens have moved online, parents have projected their fears onto the Internet, imagining all the [[31]] dangers that youth might face —from [[32]] strangers to
cruel peers to pictures or words that could haunt them on Google for the rest of their lives.

Rather than helping teens develop strategies for negotiating public life and the risks of [[33]] with others, fearful parents have focused on tracking, monitoring and blocking. These tactics(策略)don’t help teens develop the skills they need to manage complex social situations, [[34]] risks and get help when they’re in trouble. “Protecting” kids may fell like the right thing to do, but it [[35]] the learning that teens need to do as they come of age in a technology-soaked world.

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation: J) philosophy 语法判断:此处是固定短语putsth.intopractice(将....付诸实践),而空格处应填入的单词被前面的指 示代词this所修饰,故应填入单数名词或不可数名调,充当put的宾语。符合语法条件的名词选项有: influence(影响)、interpretation(翻译;诠释;演绎)、philosophy(哲学;理念;处事原则)和potential(潜 力,潜质)。 语义判断:文章开篇提到了尼采的名言,“消灭不了我们的东西会让我们变得更加强大”。空格所在句 是以but开头的转折句,结合本句中的parents can'thandleit可知,后面when引导的时间状语从句(暗 含着条件的意味)说的应该是青少年把尼采的那种哲学理念付诸实践的情况,因为这种情况(即孩子乘 持那种理念)才会使父母束手无策。所以空格处应填入philosophy,表示"理念"。下一句提到的技术领域 已经沦为大人们和他们追求自由的孩子之间旷日持久的较量的新战场也印证了这一点。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation: I) mirrors 语法判断:空格前是名词性从句Whattheydo online和频度副词often,空格后是名词性从句whatthey mightotherwisedo,由此可知,空格处应填入一个第三人称单数的动词,充当连接两个名词性从句的谓 语。符合语法条件的备选项有contains(包含,包括;控制,阻止)、mirrors(反映;映射)和undermines (损害,破坏;削弱)。 语义判断:结合第一段最后一句和本段第一句可知,本段承接上文,讲述新技术时代受到种种限制的 青少年转向社交媒体和手机,通过这些途径满足社交需求。由此可以推知,如果没有管教严格的父母 对于孩子的种种限制,青少年在网上的活动将“反映出"另外一番景象,将符合语法条件的备选项代入 文中可知mirrors最符合题意,故为答案。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation: B)constrained 语法判断:空格前是iftheirmobilityweren't so heavily,空格后是介调短语intheageofhelicopter parenting,由此可知,空格处应填入一个形容词或分词,构成系表结构或被动语态。符合语法条件的备 选形容词有constrained(拘泥的,被迫的)、potential(潜在的)和violent(暴力的),分调有interacting(互 动;相互影响)、magnified(放大)、sneaking(偷偷溜出)和sticking(坚持;粘)。 语义判断:结合上一题的分析,由本段首句提到的“青少年被禁铜在家,凭借社交媒体和手机与同龄人 交往”的内容判断,此处是说,在这个父母对子女过分关切,如同直升机盘旋在孩子头顶的年代里,孩 子们的一举一动都受到严格限制。将符合语法条件的选项代入文中可知,constrained符合文意,故为 答案。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation: D)explore 语法判断:空格前是Theywanthefreedomto,空格后是名词短语theiridentityandtheworld around them,可知此处应填入一个动词原形,构成动词不定式短语来充当后置定语,修饰freedom。符合语法 条件的动词原形选项有assess(评估)、explore(探索)和influence(影响)。 语义判断:由上一句的内容“社交媒体和智能手机应用程序近年来变得极其流行,因为青少年需要一 个属于他们自己的世界"可知,本句承接上文,继续解释青少年流行使用社交媒体和智能手机应用程 ·2015年6月六级真题(第二套)· 序的原因,即他们想要获得“探索”自我和周图世界的自由,备选项中explore符合文意,故为答案。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation: L) sneaking 语法判断:空格前是介词短语insteadof,空格后是副词out,由此可知,空格处应填入动名词。符合语 法条件的动名词选项有interacting、Sneaking和sticking。 语义判断:结合上一题的分析,根据本句中后面部分的theyjumponline可知,能与jumponline相对应 的是以前孩子们遣受限制时常用的“偷偷溜出家门"的策略,即以前行动受限时只能采取“偷偷溜走”的 办法,现在却可以通过网络与外界沟通。符合语法条件的备选动名调中sneaking符合文意,故为答案。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation: K)potential 语法判断:空格前是限定词allthe,空格后是名词dangers,由此可知,空格处应填入形容词,修饰 dangers。符合语法条件的备选形容词还有potential和violent。 知,此处是imagining引出的现在分词短语作伴随状语,进一步解释父母们如何担忧孩子的情况,将符 合语法条件的两个备选形容词代入文中,显然,potential符合文意,故为答案。potentialdangers指的是 “潜在的危险"。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation: O)violent 语法判断:由空格后的cruel peers可知,空格处应填入一个形容词修饰strangers,与cruel peers并列, 构成fromAtoB的结构。符合语法条件的形容词选项只剩下了violent。 语义判断:本句中含有破折号,可知其后面的内容是对前面内容的进一步解释,前面提到“潜在的危 险”,可知破折号后列举的是几个潜在危险的例子,violent strangers意为“暴力的陌生人”,与后面的 “cruelpeers(性情残忍的同龄人)"构成并列关系,符合上下文语境,故violent为答案。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation: F)interacting 语法判断:空格前是therisksof,空格后是withothers,由此可知,空格处应填入动名词,充当介调of 的宾语。符合语法条件的备选动名调还有interacting和sticking。 语义判断:本文旨在探讨信息时代父母和孩子之间的关系,又由下一句中的内容“这些策略无法帮助 青少年培养应对复杂社会情形..所需的各种技能”可知,此处是说父母做得不够恰当的地方,即“忧 心仲仲的父母没有帮助青少年培养应对公共生活以及与人交往的风险的能力”,将备选项代入原文, 可知interacting符合文意,为答案。interactwith意为“与互动,与..交往”。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation: A)assess 语法判断:分析句子结构可知,本句不定式中包含三个并列的动词原形,空格处应填入的动词原形与 manage和get构成并列关系。符合语法条件的动词原形备选项还有assess和influence。 语义判断:三个并列动词短语中的第一个是managecomplex social situations,第二个是 risks, 第三个是gethelp,由此不难判断,备选动词原形中assess符合文意,assessrisks意为“评估风险”,能 够与managecomplexsocial situations(应对复杂社会情形)构成并列关系。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation: N) undermines 语法判断:空格前是butit,空格后是thelearning,由此可知,but分句中缺少谓语动词,由于主语it为 第三人称单数,故所填词应为动词第三人称单数形式。符合语法条件的备选动词还有contains和 undermines。 语义判断:上文提到父母跟踪、监视和压制孩子的做法无法帮助他们培养所需技能,本句前半句提到, “保护"孩子可能感觉像是正当之举,然后用but引出转折的含义,由此可知,此处是说,这种“保护"对 具备的知识,故undermines符合文意,为答案。

sections.title: 长篇匹配
paragraphs: A) An dangerous trend has developed over this past third of a century. A country that experienced shared growth after World WarIIbegan to tear apart, so much so that when the Great Recession hit in late 2007, one could no longer ignore the division that had come to define the American economic landscape. How did this “shining city on a hill” become the advanced country with the greatest level of inequality?

B) Over the past year and a half, The Great Divide, a series in The New York Times, has presented a wide range of examples that undermine the notion that there are any truly fundamental laws of capitalism. The dynamics of the imperial capitalism of the 19th century needn’t apply in the democracies of the 21st. We don’t need to have this much inequality in America.

C) Our current brand of capitalism is a fake capitalism. For proof of this go back to our response to the Great Recession, where we socialized losses, even as we privatized gains. Perfect competition should drive profits to zero, at least theoretically, but we have monopolies making persistently high profits. C. E. O. s enjoy incomes that are on average 295 times that of the typical worker, a much higher ratio than in the past, without any evidence of a proportionate increase in productivity.

D) If it is not the cruel laws of economics that have led to America’s great divide, what is it? The straightforward answer: our policies and our politics! People get tired of hearing about Scandinavian success stories, but the fact of the matter is that Sweden, Finland and Norway have all succeeded in having about as much or faster growth in per capita(人均的)incomes than the United States and with far greater equality.

E) So why has America chosen these inequality-enhancing policies? Part of the answer is that as World War II faded into memory, so too did the solidarity it had created. As America triumphed in the Cold War, there didn’t seem to be a real competitor to our economic model. Without this international competition, we no longer had to show that our system could deliver for most of our citizens.

F) Ideology and interests combined viciously. Some drew the wrong lesson from the collapse of the Soviet system in 1991. The pendulum swung from much too much government there to much too little here. Corporate interests argued for getting rid of regulations, even when those regulations had done so much to protect and improve our environment, our safety, our health and the economy itself.

G) But this ideology was hypocritical(虚伪的). The bankers, among the strongest advocates of laissez-faire(自由放任的)economics, were only too willing to accept hundreds of billions of dollars from the government in the aid programs that have been a recurring feature of the global economy since the beginning of the Thatcher- Reagan era of “free” markets and deregulation.

H) The American political system is overrun by money. Economic inequality translates into political inequality, and political inequality yields increasing economic inequality. So corporate welfare increases as we reduce welfare for the poor. Congress maintains subsidies for rich farmers as we cut back on nutritional support for the needy. Drug companies have been given hundreds of billions of dollars as we limit Medicaid benefits. The banks that brought on the global financial crisis got billions while a tiny bit went to the homeowners and victims of the same banks’ predatory(掠夺性的) lending practices. This last decision was particularly foolish. There were alternatives to throwing money at the banks and hoping it would circulate through increased lending.

I) Our divisions are deep. Economic and geographic segregation have immunized those at the top from the problems of those down below. Like the kings of ancient times, they have come to perceive their privileged positions essentially as a natural right.

J) Our economy, our democracy and our society have paid for these gross inequalities. The true test of an economy is not how much wealth its princes can accumulate in tax havens(庇护所),but how well off the typical citizen is. But average incomes are lower than they were a quarter-century ago. Growth has gone to the very, very top, whose share has almost increased four times since 1980. Money that was meant to have trickled(流淌)down has instead evaporated in the agreeable climate of the Cayman Islands.

K) With almost a quarter of American children younger than 5 living in poverty, and with America doing so little for its poor, the deprivations of one generation are being visited upon the next. Of course, no country has ever come close to providing complete equality of opportunity. But why is America one of the advanced countries where the life prospects of the young are most sharply determined by the income and education of their parents?

L) Among the most bitter stories in The Great Divide were those that portrayed the frustrations of the young, who long to enter our shrinking middle class. Soaring tuitions and declining incomes have resulted in larger debt burdens. Those with only a high school diploma have seen their incomes decline by 13 percent over the past 35 years.

M) Where justice is concerned, there is also a huge divide. In the eyes of the rest of the world and a significant part of its own population, mass imprisonment has come to define America—a country, it bears repeating, with about 5 percent of the world’s population but around a fourth of the world’s prisoners.

N) Justice has become a commodity, affordable to only a few. While Wall Street executives used their expensive lawyers to ensure that their ranks were not held accountable for the misdeeds that the crisis in 2008 so graphically revealed, the banks abused our legal system to foreclose(取消赎回权)on mortgages and eject tenants, some of whom did not even owe money.

O) More than a half-century ago, America led the way in advocating for the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations in 1948. Today, access to health care is among the most universally accepted rights, at least in the advanced countries. America, despite the implementation of the Affordable Care Act, is the exception. In the relief that many felt when the Supreme Court did not overturn the Affordable Care Act, the implications of the decision for Medicaid were not fully appreciated. Obamacare’s objective —to ensure that all Americans have access to health care—has been blocked: 24 states have not implemented the expanded Medicaid program, which was the means by which Obamacare was supposed to deliver on its promise to some of the poorest.

P) We need not just a new war on poverty but a war to protect the middle class. Solutions to these problems do not have to be novel. Far from it. Making markets act like markets would be a good place to start. We must end the rent-seeking society we have gravitated toward, in which the wealthy obtain profits by manipulating the system.

Q) The problem of inequality is not so much a matter of technical economics. It’s really a problem of practical politics. Inequality is not just about the top marginal tax rate but also about our children’s access to food and the right to justice for all. If we spent more on education, health and infrastructure(基础设施), we would strengthen our economy, now and in the future.

questions.stem: In theory, free competition is supposed to reduce the margin of profits to the minimum.
questions.explanation: C 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词intheory、freecompetition和profits。文章段落中C段提到自由竞争和 ·2015年6月六级真题(第二套)· 利润的关系,该段第三句提到,最好的竞争应该使盈利为零,至少在理论上是如此,但我们的望断部门 仍在不断地获得高收益。所以,题干是对原文的同义转述。perfectcompetition即“自由竞争”,对应题干 中的freecompetition。使利润为零,即将利润率降至最低,所以原文中的shoulddriveprofitsto zero对应 题干中的issupposedtoreducethemarginofprofitstotheminimum。对于“理论上",原文中用的是副词 theoretically,对应题干中的介词短语intheory。

questions.stem: The United States is now characterized by a great division between the rich and the poor.
questions.explanation: A 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词characterized和agreatdivision。文章段落中A段提到美国社会有巨大 鸿沟的特征。该段第二句指出,一个在二战后经历过共同发展的国家开始分裂,以至于当2007年经济 大萧条出现的时候,人们没法再对定义美国经济面貌的贫富分化视而不见。因此,题干是对原文的同 义概括。题干中的ischaracterizedby对应原文中的define;题干中的agreatdivisionbetweentherichand thepoor对应原文中的division,这里的division指的就是巨大的贫富分化。

questions.stem: America lacked the incentive to care for the majority of its citizens as it found no rival for its economic model.
questions.explanation: E 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词care forthemajority of its citizens和foundno rival forits economic model。文章段落中论及美国经济模式的内容出现在E段。该段第三、四句话提到,随着美国在冷战中 获胜,我们的经济模式似乎已没有真正的竞争对手。没有了这种国际竞争,我们就不再需要表明我们 的体制能够对大多数公民负责。因此,题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的themajorityofitscitizens对 应原文中的mostofourcitizens,题千中的itfoundnorival foritseconomicmodel对应原文中的there didn't seem to be a real competitor to our economic modelo

questions.stem: The wealthy top have come to take privileges for granted.
questions.explanation: I 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词thewealthytop和takeprivilegesforgranted。文章段落中论及上层阶级 享有特权的是I段。该段第二、三句指出,经济和地理上的隔离使得上层阶级得以摆脱下层阶级所面临 的问题。就像古时候的国王一样,他们把自己的特权地位本质上视为自然赋予的权利。因此,题干是对 原文的同义概括。题干中的thewealthytop即原文中的thoseatthetop;原文中的perceivetheir privileged positions essentiallyasanatural right"把自己的特权地位本质上视为自然赋予的权利"意思就 是“想当然地享有特权”,即题干中的takeprivilegesforgranted。

questions.stem: Many examples show the basic laws of imperial capitalism no longer apply in present- day America.
questions.explanation: B 解析:注意抓住题千中的关键词manyexamples、imperialcapitalism和applyinpresent-dayAmerica。文 章段落中论及国资本主义基本法则的是B段。该段前两句提到,在过去的一年半里,《纽约时报》进 行的“巨大的鸿沟"系列报道给出了大量例子以动摇存在真正的资本主义基本法则这一观点。19世纪帝 国资本主义的动力机制并不适用于21世纪的民主政体。因此,题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 manyexamples对应原文中的awiderangeofexamples,题干中的thebasiclawsofimperialcapitalism对 应原文中的fundamentallawsofcapitalism,题干中的applyin是原词重现。

questions.stem: The author suggests a return to the true spirit of the market.
questions.explanation: P 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词theauthorsuggests和thetrue spiritofthemarket。文章段落中P段论及 作者对于通过市场运作以解决贫富差距的建议。该段前几句指出,我们需要的不只是一场针对贫困的 新战争,而是一场保护中产阶级的战争。解决这些问题的方法不必新奇,远远不必。让市场自如运作将 是个不错的开头。因此,题干是对原文的同义概括。原文中的makingmarketsactlikemarkets"让市场自 如运作"即题干中所说的aretumtothetruespiritofthemarket"回归到市场的真正精神"。

questions.stem: A quarter of the world’s prisoner population is in America.
questions.explanation: M 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词aquarteroftheworld'sprisonerpopulation。文章段落中论及世界四犯数 量的内容出现在M段。M段第二句后半部分提到,算上重复入获的人数,美国有着约为世界5%的人 口,但是囚犯的数量却约占世界的四分之一。因此,题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的aquarterof the world's prisoner population对应原文中的a fourth of the world's prisoners。

questions.stem: Government regulation in America went from one extreme to the other in the past two decades.
questions.explanation: F 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词govemmentregulationin America。文章段落中论及美国政府干预的内 容出现在F段。该段第二、三句指出,有人吸取了1991年苏联体制瓦解的错误教训,政府干预经济的 力度从以前的太大变成现在的太小。因此,题干是对原文的同义概括。从以前过多的政府干预转变为现 在的较少管制,即政府干预从一个极端走向了另一个极端。题干中的wentfromoneextremetothe other 对应原文中的swungfrommuchtoomuch...tomuchtoo little...o

questions.stem: Justice has become so expensive that only a small number of people like corporate executives can afford it.
questions.explanation: N 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词justice、expensive、asmallnumberofpeople和afford。文章段落中论及司 法昂贵的内容出现在N段。该段第一句指出,司法已成为一种商品,只有少数人才消费得起。后文便以华 尔街高管为例加以说明。因此,题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的justice、expensive和executives属于 原词重现,题干中的onlyasmallnumberofpeople.anaffordit对应原文中的affordabletoonlyafew。 ·2015年6月六级真题(第二套)·

questions.stem: No country in the world so far has been able to provide completely equal opportunities for all.
questions.explanation: K 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词providecompletelyequalopportunitiesforall。文章段落中论及能够为所 有人提供完全平等机会的国家的内容出现在K段。该段第二句指出,当然,没有一个国家能达到提供 近乎完全平等的机会的目标。因此,题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的nocountry是原词重现;题干 中的sofar对应原文中的ever;题千中的hasbeen ableto providecompletelyequal opportunitiesforall对 应原文中的comeclose to providing complete equality of opportunity。

sections.title: 仔细阅读 · 1
paragraphs: I’ll admit I’ve never quite understood the obsession (难以破除的成见) surrounding genetically modified (GM) crops. To environmentalist opponents, GM foods are simply evil, an understudied, possibly harmful tool used by big agricultural businesses to control global seed markets and crush local farmers. They argue that GM foods have never delivered on their supposed promise, that money spent on GM crops would be better channeled to organic farming and that consumers should be protected with warning labels on any products that contain genetically modified ingredients. To supporters, GM crops are a key part of the effort to sustainably provide food to meet a growing global population. But more than that, supporters see the GM opposition of many environmentalists as fundamentally anti-science, no different than those who question the basics of man-made climate change.

For both sides, GM foods seem to act as a symbol: you’re pro-agricultural business or anti-science. But science is exactly what we need more of when it comes to GM foods, which is why I was happy to see Nature devote a special series of articles to the GM food controversy. The conclusion: while GM crops haven’t yet realized their initial promise and have been dominated by agricultural businesses, there is reason to continue to use and develop them to help meet the enormous challenge of sustainably feeding a growing planet.

That doesn’t mean GM crops are perfect, or a one-size-fits-all solution to global agriculture problems. But anything that can increase farming efficiency—the amount of crops we can produce per acre of land—will be extremely useful. GM crops can and almost certainly will be part of that suite of tools, but so will traditional plant breeding, improved soil and crop management—and perhaps most important of all, better storage and transport infrastructure(基础设施), especially in the developing world. (It doesn’t do much good for farmers in places like sub-Saharan Africa to produce more food if they can’t get it to hungry consumers.) I’d like to see more non-industry research done on GM crops—not just because we’d worry less about bias, but also because seed companies like Monsanto and Pioneer shouldn’t be the only entities working to harness genetic modification. I’d like to see GM research on less commercial crops, like corn. I don’t think it’s vital to label GM ingredients in food, but I also wouldn’t be against it—and industry would be smart to go along with labeling, just as a way of removing fears about the technology.

Most of all, though, I wish a tenth of the energy that’s spent endlessly debating GM crops was focused on those more pressing challenges for global agriculture. There are much bigger battles to fight.

questions.stem: How do environmentalist opponents view GM foods according to the passage?

options.text: They will eventually ruin agriculture and the environment.
They are used by big businesses to monopolize agriculture.
They have proved potentially harmful to consumers’ health.
They pose a tremendous threat to current farming practice.

questions.explanation: B 定位:根据题干的信息词environmentalistopponents,可以把答题线索定位到第一段第二句。 解析:该句提到“对于奉行环境保护主义的反对人士来说,转基因作物简直就是罪恶的,是被大型的农 业企业利用来控制全球种子市场和压迫当地农民的未经充分研究的工具”,可知反对者认为转基因作 物被大型企业用来操纵农业市场,B项符合文意,故为正确答案。文中并未明确提及转基因作物会破坏 环境,故排除A项。文中未提及有明确证据证明其对消费者的健康有害,排除C项。文中也没有提及它 们给当前农业生产造成了巨大的威胁,D项也应排除。

questions.stem: What does the author say is vital to solving the controversy between the two sides of the debate?

options.text: More scientific research on GM crops.

questions.explanation: D 定位:根据题干的信息词vitaltosolvingthecontroversy和thetwosidesofthedebate,可以把答题线索 定位到第二段前两句。 解析:第二段第一句提到“对于双方来说,转基固食品都看似成为一种象征:你是支持农业企业抑或是 反对科学”,接着作者用but转折,阐明自己的观点一—“但是说到转基因食品这个话题,科学则恰恰 ·2015年6月六级真题(第二套)· 是我们更需要的”,即作者认为应该用科学和客观的观点来看待这个问题,然后作者援引《自然》杂志一 系列文章的结论,认为虽然转基因作物有其利弊,但对当前世界的食品供应有重大意义,结合四个选 项可知D项最符合作者的观点。A项是反对者的观点,不是作者的观点,不符合题干要求,排除。B、C 两项本身说法合理,但文章并未提及,也不是作者想要表达的,均可排除。

questions.stem: What is the main point of the Nature articles?

options.text: Feeding the growing population makes it imperative to develop GM crops.
Popularizing GM technology will help it to live up to its initial promises.
Measures should be taken to ensure the safety of GM foods.
Both supporters and opponents should make compromises.

questions.explanation: A 定位:根据题干的信息词themainpointoftheNaturearticles,可以把答题线索定位到第二段第二、 三句。 解析:第二段第二句提到了《自然》杂志,接着第三句指出了杂志中文章的结论:“虽然转基因作物还 未兑现它们最初的承诺,且受农业企业的操控,却仍然有理由对其继续使用并加以开发,以帮助应 基因作物有其弊端,但有助于全球的食品供应,在应对食品短缺这一巨大挑战上意义重大,强调了 其必要性,由此可知答案为A。其他三项都无法从《自然》杂志的文章得出的结论中推断出来,均 可排除。

questions.stem: What is the author’s view on the solution to agricultural problems?

options.text: It has to depend more and more on GM technology.
It is vital to the sustainable development of human society.
GM crops should be allowed until better alternatives are found.
Whatever is useful to boost farming efficiency should be encouraged.

questions.explanation: D 定位:根据题干的信息词theauthor'sviewonthesolutiontoagricultural problems,可以把答题线索定位 到第三段第二句。 解析:题干问的是作者的观点,第三段第二句提到“但是,任何能够提高农业效率(每英亩土地的粮食 产量)的方法都将是极其有益的”,即作者认为在当前全球严峻的食品供应形势下,任何有利于提高农 业效率的方法都应该得到提倡,转基因作物也不例外,是解决农业问题的工具之一,后面还进一步列 举了其他一些工具。由此可知答案为D。文中并没有提到农业问题的解决会越来越依赖转基因技术,A 项排除。B项提及人类社会的可持续发展,范图扩大化了,应排除。C项提及了“更好的替代品”,原文 中并无相关信息,属于无中生有,也可排除。

questions.stem: What does the author think of the ongoing debate around GM crops?

options.text: It arises out of ignorance of and prejudice against new science.
It distracts the public attention from other key issues of the world.
Efforts spent on it should be turned to more urgent issues of agriculture.
Neither side is likely to give in until more convincing evidence is found.

questions.explanation: C 定位:根据题干的信息词theauthorthinkof和theongoingdebatearoundGMcrops,可以把答题线索定 位到最后一段第一句。 解析:该句提到“然而,最重要的是,我希望人们能将不断耗费在有关转基因作物的争论上的精力的十 分之一用以关注全球农业更加急迫的那些挑战”,可知作者认为人们耗费在有关转基因作物的争论上 的精力太多了,不应过于纠结该问题,全球农业还有更紧急、更迫切的问题等待解决,故答案为C项。 A项和D项文中都没有提及,可排除。B项有一定的干扰性,容易误选,但综合全文来看,本文讨论的 是农业领域的转基因问题,最后一段明确说明的是全球农业所面临的其他挑战,所以B项范围扩大化 了,应排除。

sections.title: 仔细阅读 · 2
paragraphs: Early decision—you apply to one school? and admission is binding—seems like a great choice for nervous applicants. Schools let in a higher percentage of early-decision applicants, which arguably means that you have a better chance of getting in. And if you do, you’re done with the whole agonizing process by December. But what most students and parents don’t realize is that schools have hidden motives for offering early decision.

Early decision, since it’s binding, allows schools to fill their classes with qualified students; it allows admissions committees to select the students that are in particular demand for their college and know those students will come. It also gives schools a higher yield rate, which is often used as one of the ways to measure college selectivity and popularity.

The problem is that this process effectively shortens the window of time students have to make one of the most important decisions of their lives up to that point. Under regular admissions, seniors have until May 1 to choose which school to attend; early decision effectively steals six months from them, months that could be used to visit more schools, do more research, speak to current students and alumni(校友)and arguably make a more informed decision.

There are, frankly, an astonishing number of exceptional colleges in America, and for any given student, there are a number of schools that are a great fit. When students become too fixated(专注)on a particular school early in the admissions process, that fixation can lead to severe disappointment if they don’t get in or, if they do? the possibility that they are now bound to go to a school that, given time for further reflection, may not actually be right for them.

Insofar as early decision offers a genuine admissions edge, that advantage goes largely to students who already have numerous advantages. The students who use early decision tend to be those who have received higher-quality college guidance, usually a result of coming from a more privileged background. In this regard, there’s an argument
against early decision, as students from lower-income families are far less likely to have the admissions know-how to navigate the often confusing early deadlines.

Students who have done their research and are confident that there’s one school they would be thrilled to get into should, under the current system, probably apply under early decision. But for students who haven’t yet done enough research, or who are still constantly changing their minds on favorite schools, the early-decision system needlessly and prematurely narrows the field of possibility just at a time when students should be opening themselves to a whole range of thrilling options.

questions.stem: What are students obliged to do under early decision?

options.text: Look into a lot of schools before they apply.
Attend the school once they are admitted.
Think twice before they accept the offer.
Consult the current students and alumni.

questions.explanation: B 定位:根据题干中的信息词obliged和earlydecision,可以将答案线索定位到文章第一段。 解析:解题关键在于考生能否准确理解第一句中binding一词的含义,binding在词典中的释义是“有约 束力的,捆绑的”,考生可以推断出申请学校的录取是有约束力的,结合四个选项,只有选项B能表达 出这层含义。如果考生不知道binding的释义,也可以根据第二段内容推断出该词的含义,文章第二段 第一句提到“由于..",它允许招生委员会挑选本校有特殊需求的学生,并且知道被挑中的学生会来校 报到”,考生根据结果反推原因,将四个选项分别代入,显然只有选项B符合文意。文章第三段提到“申 请之前调研很多学校"和“咨询在校生和校友”,但这都是走常规申请流程的学生的做法,而非提前申请 的学生,故排除选项A和D。选项C在文中没有提及,故排除。

questions.stem: Why do schools offer early decision?

options.text: To make sure they get qualified students.
To avoid competition with other colleges.
To provide more opportunities for applicants.
To save students the agony of choosing a school.

questions.explanation: A 定位:根据题干中的信息词offerearlydecision,可以将答案线索定位在文章第一段最后一句,但该句 只是陈述了“学校录取提前申请的学生有潜在动机”这一事实,而题干问的是这一潜在动机具体是什 么,所以我们可以将答案线索进一步定位到第二段。 解析:第二段第一句的前半部分提到“由于提前录取具有约束力,因此学校能够招满合格学生”。由此 可知,学校录取提前申请的学生的原因之一就是确保本校能招到合格的学生。选项A是对原文内容的 同义转述,故为答案。选项B在文中没有提及,需排除。选项C是根据文章第一段第二句设置的干扰 项,该句提到“学校录取提前申请的学生的比例较高,这就意味着申请者被录取的几率更大。”但这只 是表面现象,大多数学生和父母没有意识到其潜在动机,故选项C也要排除。文章第一段第三句提到 提前申请的过程很痛苦,选项D是想通过同根词(agonizing和agony)复现来误导考生,但只要仔细阅 读文章就会发现,“避免学生陷入择校的苦恼”显然不是学校提前录取学生的原因,故排除。

questions.stem: What is said to be the problem with early decision for students?

options.text: It makes their application process more complicated.
It places too high a demand on their research ability.
It allows them little time to make informed decisions.
It exerts much more psychological pressure on them.

questions.explanation: C 定位:根据题干中的信息词problemwithearlydecision,将答案线索定位到文章第三段。 解析:文章第三段由两句话构成,首句即主题句,提到“问题是,这一申请流程有效地把学生们不得不 做出一个人生重大决定的一小段时间缩短至那一刻。”第二句则通过对比,具体阐述了走常规申请流 程的学生有更多的时间做思虑更周全的决定。综上所述,提前申请给学生带来的问题是“给学生留出很 少时间来做思虑周全的决定”,选项C是对原文内容的概括,故为答案。文章提到了提前申请的流程很 复杂,但没有信息表明提前申请会使学生的申请流程更复杂,不存在这种递进关系,故排除选项A。文 中没有提到学生研究能力和心理压力方面的内容,故排除选项B和D。

questions.stem: Why are some people opposed to early decision?

options.text: It interferes with students’ learning in high school.
It is biased against students at ordinary high schools.
It causes unnecessary confusion among college applicants.
It places students from lower-income families at a disadvantage.

questions.explanation: D 定位:根据题干中的信息词opposedtoearlydecision,可以将答案线索定位到文章第五段最后一句。 解析:第五段最后一句提到“就这一点而言,有人反对提前申请,因为来自低收入家庭的学生不太可能 具备招生专业知识以指导他们弄清楚那些今人困的提前录取的截止日期。"而第五段的前半部分也 提到背景优越的学生会受到高质量的择校指导。通过对比背景优越的学生和来自低收入家庭的学生, 作者旨在说明提前申请是不公平的,因为低收入家庭的学生明显处于劣势,选项D是对原文的概括, 为正确答案。文中没有提到学生在高中学习的内容,故排除选项A。选项B是强干扰项,考生不能将 students atordinaryhighschools等同于第五段中的students fromlower-incomefamilies,普通高中的学生 并不都来自低收入家庭,来自低收入家庭的学生也不一定都上普通高中,两者不是同一个概念,故排 除选项B。线索定位句中出现了选项C中confusion一词的同根词confusing,但原文是说令人困感的截 止日期,而不是给学生带来不必要的困扰,故排除选项C。

questions.stem: What does the author advise college applicants to do?

options.text: Refrain from competing with students from privileged families.
Avoid choosing early decision unless they are fully prepared.
Find sufficient information about their favorite schools.
Look beyond the few supposedly thrilling options.

questions.explanation: B 定位:根据题干中的信息词author和advise及题文同序的原则,可以将答案线索定位到文章最后一段。 解析:文章最后一段是作者给大学申请者的建议,首句是给做好充分准备的学生的建议,即可以提前 申请院校;后一句是给没有做好准备的学生的建议,即不要提前申请院校,以免缩小了自己的择校范 围。观察四个选项,只有选项B是对第二句的全面概括,故为正确答案。文章第五段只是提到来自背景 ·2015年6月六级真题(第二套)· 优越的家庭的学生和来自低收入家庭的学生在提前申请院校方面的优劣势,作者并没有建议申请者避 免和来自特权家庭的学生竞争,故排除选项A。选项C是对做好充分准备的学生的界定,不是作者的 建议。选项D是作者针对没有做好充分准备的学生的建议之一,而题干问的是大学申请者,并没有局 限于未做好充分准备的学生,故也排除。
